en.html:
I moved into a low guard.
Sword beside my body, edge down. A stance for cutting upward.

Compared with the orthodox high guard of armored swordsmanship, some force would be missing from the stroke. That much I could not deny.
Splitting the enemy's plating with one cut would be difficult.

But I had something in mind.

ja.html:
俺は下段に移った。
　太刀を体側、刃を下に向けてとり、斬り上げてゆく
構えだ。

　武者剣術の正調たる上段と比べれば、太刀筋にやや
勢力を欠くことは否めない。
　一刀で敵騎の甲鉄を斬り割るのは難しかろう。

　しかし俺には若干、思うところがあった。

en.html:
From its high guard, the enemy would naturally pass along our belly side and swing down.
From my low guard, I had to pass along its back and cut upward.

In this kind of exchange, quick judgment and sword speed decided the matter.
Recognize the striking distance first, strike first. Victory went to that side—

en.html:
The inexplicable blow had not struck.
We passed each other and separated. No further attack.

...So this suspicious something had difficulty striking towards its own rear?

Quite possible, it seemed.
That visibly greedy enemy did not look like it would spare an attack out of courtesy. No other reason came to mind.

But I still did not know what the thing was. A convenient conclusion was not necessarily a safe one...

ja.html:
あの不可解な一撃は、俺を襲わなかった。
　それ以上の攻撃を浴びることなく敵騎と行き違い、
離れる。

　……つまりあの怪しい<ruby>何か<rt>・・</rt></ruby>は、自騎の背面方向には
繰り出しにくい性質のものなのか。

　どうもその可能性が高いようだ。
　他に、あの見るからに貪欲な敵騎が攻撃を手控える
理由というのも無さそうに思える。

　未だ実態を掴めていない以上、安易な断定は危険だ
が……。
